I measured it: standing-order baselines at y=234/266/298/330 against rules at y=244/276/308/340; the handwritten 'Nothing else has been asked of me yet.' baseline at y=456 against the rule at y=467. Rule pitch is 32px, so the type is orbiting the ruling rather than written on it. This is the single tell that reads instantly as 'text layer over wallpaper layer' and it destroys the illusion of a written page. | WHERE: Right page, entire ruled column — STANDING ORDER items I–IV (y 221–333) and the TO DO handwriting (y 444–456). Visible across the whole right half of the frame. | FIX: src/styles/journal.css:1118 `.jp-col--ruled` paints the rule at the BOTTOM of the line box: `linear-gradient(180deg, transparent calc(100% - 1px), var(--rule-ink) 0)`. Add `background-position: 0 calc(-0.5 * (var(--rule-pitch) - 1em) - 0.21em);` (or move the gradient stop by the same amount) so the rule lands exactly on the baseline. Verify by re-measuring: baseline y must equal rule y ±1px.

## journal-clues  (scored 4/10)
- [critical] The bottom card row is hard-clipped mid-sentence. Five cards ('Underwood 5, Rolls Room, 1928: e riding', 'ADVISED THAT THE LIGHT EXHIBITED', 'has spent for thirty-seven years and has', 'the counter advances whether the', 'box came from. He was in the dead') render a full, readable line at roughly 50% alpha and then the frame simply ends. The mask exists but is far too short — I measured the ramp at about 26px, i.e. one and a half lines of body text. The result is not 'the page dissolving', it is 'content is cut off', and a player will try to scroll a book. This alone caps the frame. | WHERE: y≈1030–1060 across the whole width of the lower leaf, x≈208–1660; worst at the 'Scorched Carbon' and 'Pitney Postmaster' cards. | FIX: src/styles/journal.css .journal-scroll — `--page-fade` is `clamp(0.9rem, 2.4cqh, 2.2rem)`. Then add a real affordance at the foot of the leaf — a printed catchword or a brass page-turn arrow on the fore edge — because right now nothing tells the player there is more book.
- [critical] The page is not lit. I sampled the spread: brightest point 238,225,197 at the head, darkest 221,203,168 mid-page — a 7% value range over an object occupying 60% of the frame. That is ambient fill, not a key with falloff. Consequently nothing on the page is modelled, the cards have no light side and no shadow side, and the whole spread reads as a flat cream rectangle with print on it. For a game called The Lamplight Cipher there is no lamp anywhere in frame and no pool of light on the page. | WHERE: the entire spread, x 165–1705, y 110–1085. | FIX: src/styles/journal.css .journal__vignette — the radial is `115% 135% at 18% -6%` running paper-200 → paper-400 → paper-ink 34%. Add a second, warmer multiply layer keyed off `--lamp-*` so the near corner is warm and the far corner cools toward `--moon-300`. Target a 35–40% luminance spread head-to-foot, not 7%.
- [critical] A dead zone roughly 300×470px sits at the top right of the Testimony block — bare cream paper with nothing in it but two faint ring stains. ## journal-deduction  (scored 3.8/10)
- [critical] The nine suspect cards are near-black slabs (#1e1d17 sampled at 1000,340) sitting directly on a bright ochre corkboard (#816334 sampled at 870,600). That is a ~4.5-stop value break with zero transition: no bounce light from the board onto the card's lower edge, no warm reflected fill, no cast shadow that ties them to the surface. They are not objects on a board, they are `rgba(0,0,0,0.6)` divs floating above a photograph. This one defect is what makes the whole right half read as a web page, and it is the reason the frame's luminance histogram is bimodal (43.7% of pixels below L=32, only 2.7% between L=128-175 — there is no midtone modelling anywhere). | WHERE: Entire right column, x≈890-1670, all nine .ded-suspect cards. | FIX: src/styles/journal.css .ded-suspect — abandon the ink-800/ink-900 gradient entirely. Make the suspect a mounted card on the same board: `background-color: var(--paper-300)` tea-stained stock (or a mid-value oxblood leather ~#3a2a22, NOT #1e1d17) plus `var(--grain-fine)`, and replace the box-shadow with a real seated shadow — `0 1px 0 color-mix(in srgb, var(--lamp-200) 22%, transparent)` on the top edge for the key, `0 10px 18px -6px rgba(12,8,4,.7)` for contact, and an inner warm bounce `inset 0 -14px 20px -12px color-mix(in srgb, var(--lamp-600) 20%, transparent)` on the bottom so the ochre board reads as reflecting up into it.
